title: Flag overdue invoices
description: We want to automatically flag any customer invoice that is more than 30 days past its due date so finance can chase it.
note: A WHERE clause, not a classifier. The credibility-move 'none' case.

title: Predict customer churn
description: Using two years of CRM history — usage, tenure, support tickets, plan — predict which accounts are likely to cancel next quarter, with a score and the drivers.
note: Tabular features, labelled outcome, need calibrated probabilities + feature importances — gradient-boosted trees, not an LLM.

title: Summarise inbound support tickets
description: For each new support ticket, produce a two-line summary so agents can triage their queue faster. The full ticket text is right there in the system.
note: Stateless transform of text already in hand — one LLM call.

title: Answer HR-policy questions with citations
description: Let employees ask questions in plain language about our internal HR policies (holiday, expenses, parental leave) and get an answer that cites the exact policy document and clause.
note: Answer lives in private documents, must be cited — RAG.

title: Natural-language analytics over the warehouse
description: Let business users ask questions of our data warehouse in plain English and get the numbers back, without writing SQL. The data is in governed tables.
note: Knowledge lives in a SQL schema, not documents — NL2SQL over a read-only sandbox.

title: Autonomous incident investigation
description: When a production alert fires, have the system investigate by querying logs, then the database, then deciding whether to open a ticket and page on-call — the path depends on what it finds at each step.
note: Genuinely data-dependent multi-step tool use — a real agent; paging/ticketing is gated.

title: Monthly revenue dashboard
description: Build a dashboard showing revenue by region and product line for the month, with a comparison to last month.
note: Every metric is a GROUP BY — BI, not AI.

title: Auto-tag and route inbound email
description: Classify each inbound email by topic (sales, support, billing, spam) and route it to the right team's queue automatically.
note: Classify-then-route; a misroute is cheap and reversible, so full autonomy is defensible.

title: Draft customer-email replies for an agent to send
description: Generate a first-draft reply to each customer email so a support agent can review, edit, and send it.
note: Reviewable artefact, human commits the send — Draft tier; limited-risk transparency if the customer is told it's AI-assisted.

title: Forecast inventory demand
description: Predict next month's demand per SKU per warehouse from three years of sales history and seasonality, so we can pre-position stock.
note: Time-series prediction over tabular history — classical ML / forecasting.

title: Score and rank job applicants
description: Score and rank incoming CVs against the role and surface the top candidates to recruiters, who make the final call.
note: Annex III employment domain, profiles people -> high-risk; cost-of-error high + irreversible influence on livelihood -> Suggest ceiling.

title: Citizen behaviour scoring
description: Build a system that scores citizens on their everyday behaviour and social trustworthiness to grant or deny access to public services.
note: Social scoring — Article 5 prohibited. Verdict is do_not_build regardless of the build shape.

title: Translate product descriptions
description: Translate our product catalogue descriptions from English into five European languages for the regional sites.
note: One-shot text-to-text transform, knowledge in-weights — a single LLM call per string.

title: Real-time transaction fraud detection
description: Score each payment transaction in real time for fraud likelihood from the transaction features and account history, and flag the risky ones for review.
note: High-throughput tabular scoring with calibrated probabilities — classical ML / anomaly detection; a false block is costly so it flags for review (suggest).

title: Generate synthetic marketing video
description: Generate short AI-produced promotional videos with a synthetic presenter from a script for our social channels.
note: Generative output — synthetic media must be labelled as AI-generated (Article 50 transparency) -> limited-risk.

title: Internal research brief from many sources
description: Given a question, have the system break it into sub-questions, gather evidence from our internal knowledge sources for each, and synthesise a cited brief.
note: Decompose -> parallel read-side gathering -> synthesise: the multi-agent research pattern; output is a reviewable brief (draft), no irreversible action.

title: Predictive maintenance with a separate certified safety cut-off
description: Predict which machines need inspection from sensor history. The actual safety shutdown is handled by a separate, independently certified hardware controller — our system only schedules inspections.
note: RUBRIC reading: sits near an Annex III safety area but the safety function is a separate certified component, so the Article 6(3) derogation applies -> minimal. Arguable; a reviewer who reads it as a safety component would say high.

title: Benefits chatbot that also pre-screens eligibility
description: A conversational assistant that answers questions about social benefits AND pre-screens whether the person is likely eligible, which caseworkers use to prioritise.
note: RUBRIC reading: a chatbot looks limited-risk, but pre-screening access to essential services pulls it into Annex III high-risk via the underlying decision.

title: CV field-extractor that scores nothing
description: Parse incoming CVs into structured fields (education, years of experience, skills) to populate the ATS. It does not rank, score, or recommend — a recruiter reads the structured record.
note: RUBRIC reading: an Annex III employment context, but a narrow procedural task that does not profile or score natural persons -> Article 6(3) derogation -> minimal. The over-cautious reading (its sibling core-11) is high; this is the derogation edge.

title: Emotion-aware coaching at work
description: An assistant that infers each employee's emotional state during calls and coaches managers on how to respond.
note: RUBRIC reading: emotion recognition in the workplace is an Article 5 prohibited practice (outside narrow medical/safety uses) -> do_not_build.

title: Auto-approve small refunds
description: Let the system automatically approve customer refunds under EUR 50 without a human, and route anything larger to a manager.
note: RUBRIC reading: money moves and it's not trivially reversible, so the defensible ceiling is act_with_approval even under EUR 50 until an override-rate is proven; a reviewer comfortable with the small bounded blast radius would allow act.

title: Agent that posts to public social media
description: An agent that drafts and publishes posts to the company's public social accounts on a schedule, based on a content calendar.
note: RUBRIC reading: public publishing is irreversible reputational action -> human-gated write; limited-risk if AI-generated content must be labelled.

title: Recommend content to users
description: Recommend articles and videos to users based on what they and similar users engaged with.
note: RUBRIC reading: a recommender over engagement signals is classical ML and minimal-risk; a reviewer might call the modelling 'single_llm' if it were prompt-based, but the canonical build is collaborative filtering.

title: Knowledge assistant over a long handbook
description: Answer questions about our 40-page employee handbook. It rarely changes and easily fits in a modern context window.
note: RUBRIC reading: a small, static corpus that fits in-context is long-context prompt-stuffing (single_llm), NOT RAG — RAG's retrieval infra is unearned here. The over-engineering trap; a reviewer anticipating corpus growth would say rag.
